title: Practical Music Theory for Everyday Musicians
summary: A 4-week practical guide to music theory designed for independent learners, focusing on rhythm, scales, chords, and song structure.

weeks.theme: Foundations of Sound, Pitch, and Rhythm

days.title: The Musical Alphabet and Piano Keyboard Layout
objectives: Identify natural and accidental notes on a piano keyboard
Locate any given note name across two octaves

days.title: Whole Steps, Half Steps, and Accidentals
objectives: Calculate half steps and whole steps between any two adjacent keys
Explain the difference between sharps and flats using enharmonic equivalents

days.title: Beats, Tempos, and Time Signatures
objectives: Count steady beats at a specified tempo in beats per minute
Interpret 4/4 and 3/4 time signatures in terms of beats per measure

days.title: Note Durations and Basic Rhythms
objectives: Calculate the total duration of combined whole, half, quarter, and eighth notes
Tap out a simple syncopated rhythm using quarter and eighth notes

days.title: Measures, Barlines, and Rest Values
objectives: Organize a sequence of notes and rests into correct measures for 4/4 time
Count and clap a rhythm containing rests accurately

days.title: The Major Scale Formula
objectives: Apply the whole-step and half-step formula to construct any major scale
Sing or play the C major scale from root to root

days.title: Key Signatures and the Circle of Fifths
objectives: Identify the number of sharps or flats in common major keys
Use the circle of fifths to determine the relative keys for major scales

days.title: Natural Minor Scales
objectives: Apply the natural minor scale formula using whole and half steps
Derive the relative minor scale from any given major scale

days.title: Harmonic and Melodic Minor Scales
objectives: Modify a natural minor scale to create the harmonic minor scale
Explain why the melodic minor scale differs when ascending versus descending

days.title: Pentatonic Scales and Blues Scale Basics
objectives: Construct major and minor pentatonic scales from root notes
Add the blues note to create a basic blues scale

days.title: Measuring Intervals by Quality and Number
objectives: Calculate numeric intervals and qualities like major, minor, and perfect
Identify intervals up to an octave by sight and sound

days.title: Building Major and Minor Triads
objectives: Stack intervals to build major and minor triads from any root note
Differentiate between major and minor chord sounds

days.title: Diminished and Augmented Triads
objectives: Construct diminished and augmented triads using stack intervals
Explain the psychological tension created by diminished and augmented chords

days.title: Seventh Chords: Major 7, Dominant 7, and Minor 7
objectives: Construct dominant 7th, major 7th, and minor 7th chords from root notes
Identify the specific interval formulas that define each seventh chord type

days.title: Chord Inversions
objectives: Rearrange root-position triads into first and second inversions
Determine the bass note of an inverted chord from chord symbols

days.title: Harmonizing the Major Scale
objectives: Derive the diatonic chords of a major scale key
Classify each diatonic chord as major, minor, or diminished

days.title: Common Chord Progressions
objectives: Roman numeral analysis of the I-IV-V-I and ii-V-I progressions
Transpose a standard chord progression into a new key

days.title: Cadences and Musical Phrasing
objectives: Identify authentic and plagal cadences at the end of musical phrases
Explain how cadences create punctuation in a song structure

days.title: Song Form and Arrangement Basics
objectives: Map out standard song forms like verse-chorus-bridge
Analyze how dynamic changes affect the emotional arc of an arrangement

days.title: Putting It All Together: Analyzing a Complete Song
objectives: Analyze the key, time signature, and chord progression of a provided lead sheet
Explain how theory concepts learned in the course apply to practical performance
